text:
If you only read the standings, the Kings are in trouble: 5-9-2, 12 points, near the bottom of the Pacific. Our numbers tell a kinder story. Los Angeles gets 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and by our count deserved about 18 points, not 12. That gap of nearly six points is the biggest piece of bad luck in this group of teams.

Most of it lives in the crease. Kings goalies have allowed about six and a half more goals than the shots they faced would predict, and Darcy Kuemper has had leaky nights, including Saturday's loss to Pittsburgh, the game where Sidney Crosby passed Marcel Dionne on the all-time scoring list.

The offense has a new shape. Artemi Panarin and Adrian Kempe have been together at the top, and with Alex Laferriere they get 62% of the chances and have outscored teams 8-2. Kempe's hat trick against San Jose moved him past Dustin Brown on the franchise list. Brandt Clarke, back from the hit that got Ottawa's Hayden Hodgson suspended, is talking like a player ready for a bigger role, and his pair with Erik Gustafsson is driving play.

Help is coming: Mats Zuccarello is back and Kevin Fiala is close, per Daily Faceoff. The playoff odds are 30% in our simulations. What to watch: whether the saves catch up to the process before the standings gap gets too wide to close.
headline: The Kings deserve better than their record
